prompt.en: An amplifier is followed by an equal dB loss. What comparison is valid if neither stage is overloaded?

text.en: The output is above the input because gain is applied first.

feedback.en: Equal gain and loss ratios cancel regardless of their order in this simple model.

text.en: The output is below the input because loss is applied last.

feedback.en: The loss cancels the gain; being last does not make it count more.

text.en: The output equals the dB value expressed in watts.

feedback.en: dB is a ratio, not an absolute power reading.

text.en: The output power is approximately the input power.

feedback.en: The positive and negative dB values add to zero, giving a net power ratio of one.

explanation.en: Add signed dB changes to find the net ratio, then apply it to the starting power.

prompt.en: Two signals each fall by 3 dB on the same receiver. One starts just above S9; the other is much stronger. Which conclusion follows?

text.en: They end at the same received power.

feedback.en: Equal ratios do not make different starting levels equal.

text.en: Each loses about half its received power.

feedback.en: The same dB change gives the same power ratio, regardless of starting level.

text.en: Each loses the same fixed number of watts.

feedback.en: Half of a stronger signal is a larger absolute power change.

text.en: Each drops by three whole S-units.

feedback.en: dB and S-units are different scales. Three dB is not three S-units.

explanation.en: A dB change describes a relative change, including when the display is marked above S9.
